briefHtml:
NAV S$10,360,383 (-0.34% day; listed book -1.81%)

  • Biggest mover: silver — futures ~US$64.0, down ~5.8% vs the Sep 10 settlement (live ~07:50 SGT), after SLV's -3.8% plunge on Sep 10; Sep 10 US close: SILJ -4.0%, SLVP -3.9%, GDX -3.5%.
  • Key thing: August US CPI lands tonight 8:30pm SGT — the decider for next week's Sep 15-16 FOMC, priced as a ~60% coin-flip HIKE, against an oil shock (WTI $102.93, Brent $108.28 after the US sank five Iranian tankers). Waller tied his vote to this print.

Portfolio moves (Sep 10 closes unless noted)

  • US ETFs: SILJ -4.0%, SLVP -3.9%, GDX -3.5%, VNM +0.8%.
  • Watcher flags (critical): SMIC -6.8% and Xiaomi -5.5% — verified vs Yahoo closes: actual Sep 10 moves were SMIC -2.4% and Xiaomi -1.7%; the flags measure the multi-day slide off a stale baseline (watcher skipped Sep 5-9). The slide is real: SMIC -10.3% from Aug 31, Xiaomi -8.9% from Sep 4, Tencent -6.5% from Aug 28.
  • SGX: Yanlord -2.8%, YZJ -2.3%, CDL -1.6%, DBS -0.9% (76.79); STI -0.7% to 5,729.6.
  • HK: SMIC 63.45, Xiaomi 25.92, Tencent 425.6; HSI 25,275 (-0.2%) — onshore CSI 300 fell only -0.5%, i.e. an offshore/HK de-rating.
  • Metals (live): silver US$64.01 (-5.8%), gold futures US$4,356 (-1.4%); silver has taken out the US$64.7 support.

Insider trades (SGX/HK, 7d)

  • None found for held names Sep 4-11 in public web sources. Last week's Singtel cluster (six director Change-of-Interest filings, Sep 1, likely share-based comp) remains the most recent item. None surfaced is not proof of absence.

Congress trades

  • No new filings this week — BeltwayIQ week-37 (Sep 7-13, in progress) shows 0 filings disclosed so far. Source
  • Week 36 closed quiet: 4 filings, 1 member, all sales, ~US$57k. Only named item in the window: Rep. Michael Rulli (R-OH) sold GOOGL US$50,001-100,000 (traded Aug 24).

Trump / policy watch (24-48h)

  • Iran war escalation: US sank five Iranian oil tankers; Iran attacked 10 ships near Hormuz (one seafarer killed); Trump expects the war to end after midterms (contra advisors' warnings it could run past Jan 2029) and threatened strikes on Pickaxe Mountain near Natanz. WTI $102.93 (+7.1%), Brent $108.28; US diesel record $5.85/gal.
  • IAEA reported Iran to the UN Security Council (first time in 20 years) over uranium traces at undeclared sites — uranium-theme relevant; China/Russia opposed.
  • Fed politics: Aug payrolls +162k revived the Sep 15-16 hike to ~60%; Trump demanded the Fed CUT rates or face trade retaliation; promised a US$5,000 "Trump dividend" per adult if the GOP holds Congress. August CPI tonight is the decider.
  • Canada: new EOs impose 50% tariffs on more Canadian goods effective Sep 15.
  • Plumbing: Treasury tripled longer-dated buybacks to US$6bn (landed soft, yields rose; 30y >5.3%); ECB hiked Sep 10.

Risk

  • Watcher flags: SMIC -6.8% / Xiaomi -5.5% (critical) — multi-day moves off a stale baseline; the HK-tech slide is real and continues.
  • Leveraged silver (IBKR): silver -5.8% live ≈ -8.7% equity on the line today if it holds; position ~S$144k vs ~S$56,240 loan → equity ~S$88k (was ~S$96k a week ago). Hot CPI extends the flush (BofA Q4 target US$55 vs Goldman US$85-100).
  • Oil-shock stagflation loop: Brent $108 + record diesel feeds the very CPI the Fed reacts to; pressures the SGD income sleeve via rates and margins via energy costs.
  • FX: ~35% of net worth non-SGD; USDCNY ~6.70 — oil shock is CNY-negative; watch the ~S$1.65m CNY piles.
  • Concentration: the ~62% cash pile preserved capital this week — pre-commit deployment triggers before tonight's CPI and next week's FOMC.
  • Event stack: CPI tonight → FOMC Sep 15-16 → Canada tariffs Sep 15 → BOJ Sep 17-18 → Iran headlines.

Alpha — signals, not advice

  • GDX/SILJ/SLVP + silver: real-assets sleeve ~4% vs 20% target; silver round-tripped to ~US$64 with the structural bid intact (record Q2 official gold buying, ~US$2bn weekly gold-ETF inflows). Cool CPI tonight = snap-back entry; hot CPI = final flush toward US$60-62 = aggressive add zone.
  • SMIC/Xiaomi/Tencent: SMIC -10% from Aug 31 while hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance was raised ~US$30bn to ~US$733bn (UOB Kay Hian); the wedge between AI capex fundamentals and HK prices is the widest yet. AI-bottleneck 15% vs ~1% filled; Asia barbell 10% vs ~3% — staged accumulation while the oil shock dominates.
  • US duration/TIPS (Defense sleeve): 10y at ~4.95%, a hair under the 5.0% trigger; a hot-CPI print to ≥5.0% IS the signal to start building the 15% defense sleeve into peak-hike pricing; cool CPI = stand down.

trumpWatch.title: Iran war escalation — tankers sunk, Hormuz attacks
trumpWatch.detail: US sank five Iranian oil tankers; Iran attacked 10 ships near Hormuz (one seafarer killed, one missing); US aircraft reportedly damaged at Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti base. Trump expects the war to end after the Nov midterms, contra advisors' warnings it could run past Jan 2029; threatened strikes on Pickaxe Mountain near Natanz. WTI +7.1% to $102.93, Brent $108.28; US diesel record $5.85/gal.

trumpWatch.title: IAEA reports Iran to UN Security Council (first time in 20 years)
trumpWatch.detail: 35-member board voted to report Iran over uranium traces at undeclared sites; sponsored by US/UK/France/Germany; China, Russia, Niger opposed. Direct uranium-theme relevance.

trumpWatch.title: Fed hike coin-flip into tonight's CPI; Trump pressure campaign
trumpWatch.detail: August payrolls +162k (vs ~56k expected) revived Sep 15-16 hike odds to ~60%; August CPI tonight 8:30pm SGT is the decider (Waller tied his vote to it). Trump publicly demanded the Fed CUT rates or face trade retaliation; promised a US$5,000 'Trump dividend' per adult (~US$1.35tn) if Republicans hold Congress, plus US$500 Obamacare rebate checks to ~1M people pre-midterms.

trumpWatch.title: Canada trade war widens — 50% tariffs on more goods from Sep 15
trumpWatch.detail: New executive orders impose 50% tariffs on additional Canadian goods effective Sep 15, on top of Canada's C$27.6bn counter-tariffs that took effect Sep 8.

trumpWatch.title: Treasury buyback tripling lands soft; ECB hikes
trumpWatch.detail: US Treasury tripled longer-dated buybacks to US$6bn but below market hopes (~US$10bn) — 10y rose to ~4.95% (highest since Oct 2023), 30y through 5.3%. ECB hiked Sep 10. AI policy churn: Treasury CIO Corcos moved off AI policy (Politico); DOJ probing Nvidia's Groq licensing deal.
